forecasts.label: Capital financing requirement
forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

news_drafts.headline: High Peak forecasts £1.51m General Fund overspend for 2026/27 after first quarter
news_drafts.lead:
High Peak Borough Council's Executive was told that the council's main day-to-day budget, the General Fund, is forecast to end 2026/27 with a £1,512,050 overspend against budget, after funding and reserves (money set aside) have been allocated. The figure is the provisional outturn (the expected final position for the year) at the end of the first quarter.

The council's separate housing account, the housing revenue account (the ring-fenced account for its own housing stock, paid for by rents), is forecast to run a deficit of £5,446,056, which is £245,206 more than budgeted. Net interest costs, the gap between what the council pays on borrowing and earns on investments, are £62,820 over budget. At the end of the quarter the council held £17 million in cash investments and owed £74.3 million in external borrowing.

On spending on things that last, such as buildings and equipment, the General Fund capital programme (planned spending over the next few years) has a revised 2026/27 budget of £15.436 million, including sums carried forward from earlier years. The provisional outturn is a £0.361 million overspend, about 2.3% of that budget. On income, business rates collection stood at 28.07% at 30 June 2026, against 31.00% at the same date a year earlier. The report describes that as the largest adverse variance in revenue collection.

news_drafts.headline: High Peak council kept borrowing under control in 2025/26, using its own cash to cut debt costs.
news_drafts.lead: High Peak council spent £17.1m on capital projects in the year to March 2026, of which £12.1m came from external grants and contributions. The remaining £4.95m borrowing need was funded through the council's own cash reserves — a practice known as internal borrowing that saved £72,488 in interest costs. The council held £12.1m in total external debt at year-end. However, deploying reserves this way left the council with less cash to invest: its investment portfolio fell from an average of £17.5m during the year to £9.4m by the end of March, costing £74,676 in foregone investment income. The council remained within its statutory borrowing limits, with all borrowing confined to capital spending. A separate service investment — a loan to Your Housing Limited — generated £307,000 in interest income as budgeted.

findings.paper_title: Annual Treasury Management Report 2025/26, 28/07/2026 Audit & Regulatory Committee
findings.headline: Investment income fell £76,981 short of budget despite 3.78% average return
findings.detail: The council's investment portfolio averaged £20.3 million held with six institutions, achieving a 3.78% return. However, investment income fell £76,981 short of the budgeted amount for the general fund.
findings.matters: Finance directors monitor whether reserve-based investment income meets budget expectations, as shortfalls affect available general fund resources and signal cash management performance.
findings.quote: The average investment portfolio held during the year was £20.3million held with six institutions yielding an average interest rate return of 3.78%. A provisional shortfall of £76,981 is reported against the general fund budget.

findings.paper_title: Annual Treasury Management Report 2025/26, 28/07/2026 Audit & Regulatory Committee
findings.headline: Borrowing costs £160,497 over budget in 2025/26
findings.detail: The council's actual borrowing costs exceeded the budgeted amount by £160,497 during the year. Total external debt at year-end was £69.3 million.
findings.matters: Finance directors track treasury costs and budget variances as indicators of treasury performance and to identify whether rate movements or policy decisions require plan adjustments.
findings.quote: Provisional overall borrowing costs are £160,497 overspent against the budget.

findings.paper_title: Treasury Management Update Q1 2026/27, 28/07/2026 Audit & Regulatory Committee
findings.headline: General fund borrowing costs £11,740 under budget; HRA £30,910 over in Q1 forecast
findings.detail: The council's borrowing costs are tracking mixed: general fund performing £11,740 better than budget forecast, while HRA performing £30,910 worse. Total council debt stands at £74.3m with an average borrowing rate of 3.92%.
findings.matters: Debt service cost management shows treasury effectiveness; the split between general fund savings and HRA overspend indicates different financial pressures across council services, which lenders monitor to understand service-level risks.
findings.figures: General fund underspend £11,740; HRA overspend £30,910; total debt £74.3m; average annual borrowing rate 3.92%
findings.quote: Borrowing costs on the general fund are forecast to be underspent by £11,740 on the general fund and overspent by £30,910 on the HRA.

findings.paper_title: Treasury Management Update Q1 2026/27, 28/07/2026 Audit & Regulatory Committee
findings.headline: Investment income forecast to fall short by £165,860 in 2026/27
findings.detail: The council's average investment balances of £14.9m across five institutions are projected to generate income £165,860 below budget, comprising £74,560 shortfall on the general fund and £91,300 on the HRA. This represents a material cash flow pressure from lower-than-expected investment yields.
findings.matters: A significant investment income shortfall indicates the council's cash position is tighter than budgeted; lenders and peer councils track such variances to understand treasury yield pressures in the current economic environment.
findings.figures: £165,860 total shortfall; £74,560 general fund; £91,300 HRA; £14.9m average investment balances; £17m portfolio at quarter-end across five institutions
findings.quote: A shortfall of £165,860 (£74,560 general fund, £91,300 HRA) in investment income is forecast.

findings.paper_title: High Peak Borough Council Audit Plan 25-26, 02/06/2026 Audit & Regulatory Committee
findings.headline: No significant value for money weaknesses identified in arrangements assessment
findings.detail: The auditor's risk assessment of the council's arrangements to secure economy, efficiency and effectiveness in its use of resources has not identified any significant weakness areas or related risks for 2025/26.
findings.matters: Absence of significant VFM weakness findings indicates the auditor considers governance, financial planning and service delivery arrangements to be adequate
findings.quote: Our risk assessment regarding your arrangements to secure value for money has not identified any significant weakness areas or related risks.
